provider: Air Cluster — commercial product that advertises combining several accounts (incl. accounts from the same provider)

free_tier.stated: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'

egress.terms: Client-side; files are read from each provider directly. Optional client-side encryption.

tooling: Windows desktop app (AirCluster-Installer.exe). No API, no Linux, no rclone backend.
chaining: N accounts, including N accounts of the same provider, presented as one large-capacity 'cluster'.
limits_note: Whether it stripes a single large file or only spreads files across accounts is not stated on the page, and for a Windows GUI tool the answer is almost certainly file-level.
reliability_note: Closed-source commercial; cannot audit placement or repair behaviour.

evidence.proved: 'Can I use multiple accounts from the same provider? Yes... combine their capacity into one single cluster'; 'manage the total space as if it were a single, large-capacity hard drive' — the vendor's own copy, quoted verbatim; it describes several accounts combined into one pool

notes: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'

dead_end.why: 'Air Cluster allows you to add several accounts from the same server (e.g., three different OneDrive accounts) and combine their capacity into one single cluster.'
